topic.title: What if the Panama Canal ran out of water?
topic.map_answer: the lake in the middle of the isthmus that every ship crosses, shrinking on the map as the rain stops, and the long detour route drawn round the bottom of South America when it can no longer be crossed

shape.name: The drain
shape.beats: hook: the shortcut on the map and the question -> it nearly happened, a figure the viewer can count -> where its water sits on the map and where every crossing spills it -> what fills it -> the rain stops: the lake shrinks step by step, the queues grow at both ends -> the turn: the long way round, drawn on the map -> payoff: how much of the world's sea trade rides on that rain -> loop
shape.why: a what-if where one thing running out at one spot on the map (a lake) pushes the world's ships onto a route thousands of kilometres longer

title: Why can't the Panama Canal work without rain?
description:
The Panama Canal, the shortcut between two oceans, depends on a lake, and the lake depends on rain.
What happens to the world's ships if the rain stops, on the map.
Sources: MAX Security, IMF (Dec 2023). The characters are not advisers.
Maps simplified. Borders as recognised by the country each video is about.
